summary:
Jigawa State's own criminal layer is the Sharia Penal Code Law 2000, Law No. 12 of 2000, signed into law on 18 December 2000 and brought into operation on 27 December 2000 (Jigawa State Gazette Vol. 1 No. 12). It stands under Nigeria's national framework rather than replacing it, and it adds offences the national code does not reach.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on Nigeria (June 2025) lists Jigawa in a twelve-state table of Sharia penalties: for male same-sex conduct, married men face death by stoning, while unmarried men face 100 lashes and imprisonment of up to one year; same-sex acts between women carry up to 50 lashes and imprisonment of up to six months. The June 2025 note confirms that the Sharia penal layer remains the operative criminal frame for Muslims in Jigawa.

The sourcebook places Jigawa among four states, with Gombe, Kano and Zamfara, whose sodomy offence punishes unmarried men with 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm); lesbianism carries up to 50 lashes plus up to six months' imprisonment, and Jigawa's code includes the 'unnatural fusion of the female sexual organs' explanation of the offence. The code criminalises conduct the federal code does not reach, including women's same-sex conduct.

Human Rights Watch (2004) records Zamfara's governor as the first to extend Sharia to criminal law, introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000. By 2002 twelve northern states, Jigawa among them, had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation, to date the only states where Sharia courts have jurisdiction to try criminal cases.
tangentialFactors:
Jigawa's Sharia layer is one of twelve northern state regimes of the same design, so the penalties documented for Jigawa mirror those recorded for Kano, Zamfara and the other states in the Home Office table.

The stoning and lashing penalties attach to conduct that is also criminalised nationally under the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014, so a visitor in Jigawa faces both layers at once, with the Sharia court the forum for Muslim defendants.
localsOnly:
For Muslim residents of Jigawa, the Sharia Penal Code Law 2000 is the operative criminal frame, and Sharia courts hold jurisdiction over criminal cases — a jurisdictional feature that Human Rights Watch (2004) records as unique to these twelve northern states.

The code's coverage of women's same-sex conduct, including the 'unnatural fusion of the female sexual organs' provision, reaches further than the federal code, exposing female residents to penalties the national statute does not provide for.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not document any prosecution, sentence or enforcement action under Jigawa's Sharia Penal Code Law 2000; the penalties are sourced from the statute as listed in the Home Office note and the sourcebook, and no case-level application is recorded here.

No Jigawa-specific incident of violence, arrest or police conduct against a trans or gender-nonconforming person is documented in this inventory; the incidents in the national record occurred in other states.

Whether a non-Muslim resident of Jigawa falls under the Sharia penal layer or only the federal code is not resolved in these sources.
